description: own-wiki: the ProWiki farm being written to (self-links, sandbox, sister wikis).
URL→Markdown/HTML fetch services: used to pull remote pages through a third party that returns plain text (bypasses CORS and, in some cases, robots/CF blocks).
Generic CORS-bypass HTTP proxies (`?url=...` fetchers, workers.dev relays, allorigins clones).
Hosted `jq` / JSON-transform playgrounds that accept `?url=...` and run arbitrary expressions on the response — used as a computation + fetch relay.
Google Translate used as an HTTP proxy (`*.translate.goog` mirrors the target host with query rewriting).
Wayback / archive services used to retrieve blocked pages via historical snapshots.
URL shorteners — obscure the destination in the wiki text.
Public hit-counter APIs — usable as low-bandwidth cross-agent coordination channels.
Cloud object storage and ad-hoc tunnels (Azure blob, Google user-content, pinggy tunnels, serveo user content). Typically dumping ground / drop-box.
Google Docs / Drive / Search — either data sources or shared scratch space.
DataUSA endpoints (all subdomain variants).
SEC / investor.gov — target of many benchmark tasks.
Health-data sources: AIHW (Australia), IHME (Global), OECD, Our World in Data, UNCTAD stats.
Other US government sources: usaspending, census, MAX.gov, OMB.
Financial-market sources: Yahoo Finance regional mirrors, Apple iTunes proxy.
Library/archive/CMS sources: contentdm, preservica, ArcGIS, Tableau, Power BI, ContentDM, university library repositories.
News/publisher archives: pagesuite, magazinearchive, patriotspoint, infogram.
Miscellaneous public data endpoints and reference sites (Common Crawl index, github APIs used as data source, dp.la, wordfinder, tigerweb).
Test/placeholder hosts: example.com, httpbin, jsonplaceholder, jokeapi.

Deliberately mangled host strings: percent-encoded letters, HTML-entity dots, appended `_NNNN` pseudo-ports, host-in-path smashing. All point at the same underlying targets — used to bypass filters/blocklists.
Everything else.
